summary: WebSocket reconnect replays leading tokens and drops trailing clause in multi-chunk responses
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports that when their client reconnects to the WebSocket streaming endpoint after a short network blip, the first 1-3 tokens of the resumed stream are duplicated and the concluding clause of long multi-chunk generations is sometimes missing (sentence cut off). Impact: ClarionDocs' end-user summarization feature produces repeated leading words and occasionally an incomplete final sentence for ~4% of sessions during reconnects; user-visible and affecting quality SLAs.

Environment details: Dedicated cluster for ClarionDocs in us-east-1, using reserved capacity with edge termination behind CloudFront and a custom NGINX reverse-proxy in their VPC. Client uses our JS SDK v1.8.2 with automatic resume logic. Problem first observed after a spike in transient edge 502s on 2026-02-19 22:10 UTC.

Observed vs expected: Observed: resumed stream emits duplicate prefix tokens (e.g., "In conclusion In conclusion,") and in ~40% of those cases the final clause or last 6-12 tokens of the completion are missing (cut mid-sentence). Expected: resume should continue exactly where left off with no duplication and full completion emitted.

Attachments: client network capture (clarion_stream_replay.pcap), SDK logs, CloudFront request IDs (attached below), and a short sample transcript illustrating duplication and truncation.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Use JS SDK v1.8.2 to open a WebSocket streaming session to /v1/streams with a long completion (min_tokens=60).
2) Simulate a short network interruption (~2s) or trigger an edge 502 on CloudFront, causing the client to reconnect and call resume with resume_token.
3) Observe resumed stream from server: check first 5 tokens and final 10 tokens of completion.
4) Repeat with different payloads and model variants (opt-2.7b, gptj-3b) to verify reproducibility.

Notes: Customer used automatic backoff (500ms) and immediate resume; reproduces more reliably when client reconnect occurs while server is still finalizing the last fragment before EOF.

investigation_notes:
- Initial hypothesis: double-play of cached prefix due to client resending last acknowledged fragment while server also re-emits primed KV cache tokens.
- Reproduced in our lab when emulating CloudFront idle connection reset + small client resume delay; saw duplicated tokens on resume in ~30% of runs.
- Difference from previous resume bugs: duplication occurs at token-boundary level (partial-word not split), suggesting re-emit of last committed choice fragment rather than truncated chunk duplication.
- Truncation correlated with upstream edge re-ordering: when CloudFront performs a TCP-level retry during the handoff, server believes finalization done and emits final control event, but the proxy path drops the terminal control frame (end_of_stream) and client stops reading before last buffer flush.
- We validated that serving-runtime final event (end_event) is generated in normal flow; missing only in sequences where edge retries and our internal TLS reneg negotiation occur within ~120ms window.
- SDK behavior: v1.8.2 aggressively tries to append resumed fragments and may re-request last unacknowledged chunk; this causes the server to re-emit the last fragment if not idempotency-protected.
- Related code pointers: runtime resume logic in runtime/streaming/handler.go, idempotency token handling in api/gateway/ws_resume.go, CloudFront config (support ticket capture), and sdk resume logic in sdk/js/stream-client.ts.
comments: 2026-02-20 09:15 - Support (Aisha): Acknowledged receipt. Escalating to infra/serving team. Asked customer for pcap and SDK logs.
2026-02-20 11:40 - SRE (Miguel): Reproduced locally by simulating CF idle reset. Duplication and occasional missing end_event observed. Opening runtime investigation. See GH PR note.

2026-02-20 15:02 - Customer (ClarionDocs - Elena M.): Confirmed reproduces against our production traffic; provided additional traces. Impacting ~4% of reconnections. Requesting timeline for mitigations.

2026-02-21 08:22 - Eng (Priya Shah): Hypothesis: missing end_event due to edge-level drop of final control frame during TLS reneg. Suggest adding extra acknowledgement handshake on resume to ensure server end-of-stream reaches client.

2026-02-21 16:50 - SRE (Miguel): Tested mitigation patch on staging: idempotency guard prevents duplicate re-emit, and we added explicit end-of-stream retry. Duplication rate down to <0.5% in staging tests. Preparing canary.
resolution:
Mitigation applied: 1) Server-side idempotency: resumed requests now include resume_seq idempotency check so the serving runtime will not re-emit already-acknowledged fragments. 2) End-of-stream defensive retry: the runtime now retries emitting the end_event control frame up to 2x if not ACKed by the proxy layer within 80ms. 3) SDK note: JS SDK v1.8.3 will add a 200ms debounce before re-requesting the last chunk on resume to avoid duplicate appends.

Rollout notes: Patch deployed to dedicated ClarionDocs fleet as a canary on 2026-02-21 22:00 UTC; observed reduction in both duplicate-prefix and missing-trailing-clause metrics across 12h canary. Full rollout scheduled 2026-02-23 pending extended verification.

Customer workaround: increase client-side resume backoff to >=250ms and upgrade to SDK v1.8.3 once released.

Follow-ups: create an infra runbook for detecting end_event drops (ENG-1122), audit CloudFront origin keepalive settings (OPS-449), and add e2e test that simulates edge retry+resume to catch regressions.
